Copies text to the clipboard.

Uses the async Clipboard API, with a fallback for insecure contexts (plain `http:`)

declarations.name: parseBoolean
declarations.description:
Parses a boolean attribute.

- absent → `null` (let the variant preset decide)
- `""`, `"true"`, `"on"`, `"yes"`, the attribute name → `true`
- `"false"`, `"off"`, `"no"`, `"0"` → `false`

declarations.name: parseInteger

type.text: { min: number, max: number, fallback: number }

declarations.description: Parses an integer within bounds.

declarations.name: parseEnum
declarations.description: Parses an enumerated attribute (case-insensitive).

declarations.name: parseList
declarations.description:
Parses a comma separated list of identifiers (e.g. `"preview,source"`), keeping only
allowed values, without duplicates, in the given order.

declarations.name: parseRanges
declarations.description:
Parses a line range list such as `"2,5-8, 12"` into sorted, merged ranges.

Ranges are never expanded into individual numbers, so `"1-999999999"` costs nothing.
Invalid parts are ignored. Reversed ranges (`"8-5"`) are normalized.

declarations.name: inRanges
declarations.description: Tells whether `n` falls in one of the sorted, merged ranges (binary search).

declarations.name: parseCssLength
declarations.description:
Validates a CSS length for `max-height` (e.g. `"400px"`, `"50vh"`, `"20rem"`).
Only plain lengths and percentages are accepted: no `var()`, `calc()` or keywords,
so authors cannot smuggle unexpected values.

declarations.name: cleanLabel
declarations.description:
Cleans a short display string (title, file name…): removes control characters,
collapses whitespace and caps the length.

declarations.name: cleanFileName
declarations.description:
Builds a safe download file name: strips paths, reserved characters and control
characters, and caps the length.

declarations.name: sheet
declarations.description:
Returns a constructable stylesheet for a CSS string (cached and shared).
Constructable stylesheets work under a strict `style-src` CSP.

declarations.description:
Global configuration shared by every Vitrine element.

Values set here act as defaults: attributes on an element always win.

declarations.name: configure
declarations.description:
Updates the global configuration. Unknown keys and invalid values are ignored
(a warning is logged), so a typo never breaks the page.

Connected elements re-render with the new values. They reload their content (and
fetch `src` again) only when `maxSize` changes, since it decides what may be shown.

Error with a stable code and parameters, so the UI can display a translated message.
declarations.name: VitrineError
readInlineContent
declarations.description:
Reads content written inside the element, in priority order:
a child `<template>`, a child data `<script>` (`text/plain`, `text/markdown`,
`application/json`), then the element text.

Inline content is dedented so it can be indented naturally in HTML.

Inline content is parsed by the browser as part of the page *before* Vitrine runs,
so it must never contain untrusted data: use the `content` property instead.

declarations.name: readContainer
declarations.description: Reads a content container: a `<template>` or a data `<script>`.

declarations.name: assertSize
declarations.description: Checks a content size against the configured limit.

declarations.name: fetchContent
declarations.description:
Fetches text content from a URL with origin, size and time limits.

- Only `http:` and `https:` URLs are accepted.
- Cross-origin URLs require `allowRemote`; otherwise the request runs with
  `mode: "same-origin"`, which also rejects cross-origin redirects.
- The body is streamed and the request is aborted as soon as `maxSize` is exceeded,
  so a huge response never gets fully downloaded.

declarations.name: isAbortError
declarations.description: Tells whether an error comes from a deliberate cancellation.

declarations.name: getTrustedTypesPolicy
declarations.description:
Returns the `vitrine` Trusted Types policy, creating it on first use.

The policy is private to this module and only handed to DOMPurify, so the
identity `createHTML` is never reachable with unsanitized input from outside.
Returns `null` when Trusted Types are unsupported or the policy cannot be created
(for example when the page CSP does not list `vitrine` in `trusted-types`).

declarations.name: sanitizerWorks
declarations.description:
Checks once that DOMPurify really sanitizes in this environment.

DOMPurify returns its input unchanged when it considers the environment unsupported,
and some non-browser DOM implementations make it fail silently. A known payload is
sanitized and inspected; if anything dangerous survives, every later call falls back
to plain text.

The payload holds no event handler attribute: browsers report one under a strict CSP as
soon as it is parsed, even in a detached document, and this check runs on every page.

declarations.name: sanitizeHtml
declarations.description:
Sanitizes an HTML string and returns inert DOM nodes.

The HTML is parsed by DOMPurify in a detached document with a strict allow-list,
then post-processed: unsafe URLs are removed, external links get
`rel="noopener noreferrer"`, images follow the image policy, and only
`language-*` classes are kept.

declarations.name: sanitizeHighlight
declarations.description:
Sanitizes highlight.js output: only `<span class="hljs-…">` and text survive.

highlight.js already escapes its input; this is a second, independent barrier so
that a bug in a grammar can never inject markup.

declarations.name: cleanCss
declarations.description:
Removes from CSS what could reach outside the drawing: imports, external `url()` (local
`url(#id)` references stay), escapes that could spell them, and old script hooks.

declarations.name: sanitizeDrawing
declarations.description:
Sanitizes a drawing or markup written by a library from content Vitrine does not trust
(Mermaid), and returns it as DOM, with the CSS of its `<style>` elements apart.

Inline styles are moved to CSSOM (which a strict `style-src` allows) after the same
cleaning as stylesheets; links keep only local `#id` targets; scripts, embedded
documents, external resources and attribute animations are removed.

declarations.name: sanitizeSvg
declarations.description:
Sanitizes an SVG drawing and returns its root element, with its CSS apart (for a
constructable stylesheet). See sanitizeDrawing.

declarations.name: trustedMarkup
declarations.description:
Sanitized markup ready for an `innerHTML` sink: a `TrustedHTML` from the `vitrine`
policy when Trusted Types are on, a string otherwise, without inline styles. Given as
the Trusted Types policy of the DOMPurify that Mermaid uses inside.

declarations.name: en
declarations.description:
Interface strings of <vt-calendar>, registered by its module with `defineStrings()`
so other modules do not carry them.

Displays events from an iCalendar file or JSON, as a month grid or an agenda.

Recurring events are expanded (`RRULE`, `EXDATE`, `RECURRENCE-ID`), times are shown in the
time zone of the reader or of the `timezone` attribute, and each event can be added to the
calendar of the reader as an `.ics` file. Text from the source is rendered with DOM text
APIs, and links keep safe URL schemes only.

declarations.description:
Cron expressions and crontabs: parsing, next runs in a time zone, and the parts used to
describe a schedule in words.

Fields: `[second] minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`. Five fields are the
standard; six start with seconds. Macros (`@daily`…), names (`JAN`, `MON`), lists, ranges
and steps are read, and the Quartz extensions `?`, `L`, `W` and `#` where they make sense.

declarations.name: MAX_EXPRESSION
declarations.description: Longest expression read.

declarations.name: parseCron
declarations.description: Reads a cron expression.

declarations.name: runsOn
declarations.description:
Whether a schedule runs on a date. When both the day of the month and the day of the week
are restricted, either one is enough (the cron rule); otherwise both must match.

declarations.name: isTimeZone
declarations.description: Whether a string names a time zone known to the browser.

declarations.name: civil
declarations.description: Wall-clock time of an instant in a time zone.

type.text: { year: number, month: number, day: number, hour: number, minute: number, second: number }

declarations.name: instantOf
declarations.description:
The instant of a wall-clock time in a time zone: the earlier one when the time happens
twice (clocks set back), `null` when it does not exist (clocks set forward).

declarations.name: SEARCH_DAYS
declarations.description: Days searched ahead before deciding that a schedule never runs (covers 29 February).

declarations.name: nextRuns

type.text: { from?: number, count?: number, timeZone?: string }

declarations.description:
The next times a schedule runs, after `from`.

Times that do not exist because clocks are set forward are skipped, and times that happen
twice when clocks are set back run once, at the first.

declarations.name: weekGrid
declarations.description:
How many times a schedule runs in each hour of each weekday, from its time fields and the
day of the week (`grid[weekday][hour]`, Sunday first). Restrictions on the day of the month
and the month are not reflected.

declarations.name: parseCrontab
declarations.description:
Reads a crontab: comments, `NAME=value` lines, and entries made of a schedule (five fields
or a macro), an optional user column (`system`) and a command.

declarations.name: isCrontab
declarations.description:
Whether a text is a crontab rather than one expression: several lines, comments,
variables, or a command after the schedule.

declarations.name: monthName
declarations.description:
Cron schedules in plain words, and labels of their fields, in the reader's language.
Month and weekday names come from `Intl`, so they follow the locale.

declarations.description: The schedule in words: "At 09:30, Monday through Friday".

declarations.name: describeField
declarations.description: What one field allows, for its tooltip: "minute: 0, 15 and 30".

Displays cron schedules: one expression with its fields labelled, a description in plain
words, the next runs in a time zone and the hours of the week it runs, or a whole crontab
as a table of entries with their next run and command.

declarations.name: en
declarations.description:
Interface strings of <vt-date-picker>, registered by its module with `defineStrings()`
so other modules do not carry them.

A date picker for forms: a field where the date can be typed, and a calendar to choose it
with the mouse, a finger or the keyboard. In `range` mode it chooses a period, with usual
periods such as "Last 7 days" on the side. Days can be blocked (dates, periods, days of the
week), and the first day of the week and the date format follow the language.

It takes part in `<form>` like a native field: its value is submitted under `name` as an
ISO 8601 date (`2026-11-22`) or period (`2026-11-22/2026-11-29`).

declarations.description:
Shows a diagram written in Mermaid: flowcharts, sequence, class, state and entity
relationship diagrams, Gantt charts, pie charts, mind maps, timelines, Git graphs and the
other types Mermaid draws, in the colors of the theme.

Mermaid is loaded on demand (`dist/vendor/mermaid.js`, then only the code of the types a
page uses). It runs in its strict mode: no click handlers, no HTML in labels. The SVG it
returns is sanitized again by Vitrine, its CSS goes in a constructable stylesheet without
external `url()`, and inline styles go through CSSOM, so diagrams work under a strict
Content Security Policy and Trusted Types.
declarations.name: VtDiagram

declarations.description:
Reader for configuration files: dotenv (`.env`), INI and Java `.properties`.

Every line is kept with its number. Values lose their quotes, and the escapes of
double-quoted values are decoded. `${VAR}` and `$VAR` references are listed so they
can be shown apart. Nothing is ever expanded or evaluated.

declarations.description:
Displays configuration files: dotenv (`.env`), INI and Java `.properties`, as a table of
keys and values grouped by section, with secrets masked until revealed.

Quotes, `export`, comments, multi-line quoted values and continued lines are read.
`${VAR}` references are marked, and link to the variable when it is defined in the
same file. Values whose key names a secret (`PASSWORD`, `TOKEN`, `API_KEY`…) are masked
in the table, the raw view, copy and download until the reader reveals them.

declarations.name: en
declarations.description:
Interface strings of <vt-field>, registered by its module with `defineStrings()`
so other modules do not carry them.

A form field with everything around it: a label that says when it is required, a "?"
button with help, a hint, a counter, a prefix and suffix, and clear error messages. It can
be a text input of any kind, a text area, a check box, a switch, radio buttons, check boxes,
or a list with search, groups and several choices.

It takes part in `<form>` like a native field: its value is submitted under `name`, it
blocks submission while invalid, and it is reset and disabled with the form. Options and
settings can be given as JSON.

declarations.name: topoOrder
declarations.description:
Puts commits in `git log` order, children before their parents, when the source did not:
APIs and exports often list commits oldest first, or by date only. Among the commits that
can come next, the newest comes first. Commits already in order are left as they are.

declarations.name: layoutGraph
declarations.description:
Lays commits out on lanes. Commits are in `git log` order (children before parents).
Each commit takes the lane that waits for it (the leftmost one when several children
wait), its first parent continues on that lane, and other parents get the lane that
already waits for them or the first free one.

declarations.description:
Shows a commit history as a graph: one lane per branch, merges and branch points drawn
as curves, branch and tag labels, and the hash, subject, author and date of each commit.

Reads `git log` in its default format or with `--graph`, `--oneline`, `--parents` or
`--pretty=format:'%H|%P|%an|%ad|%D|%s'`, and JSON: its own
(`[{ hash, parents, author, date, subject, refs, body, url }]`) or what the GitHub, GitLab
and Bitbucket APIs return, with branches and tags beside the commits. The lanes are computed
from the parents, after putting commits in `git log` order when the source did not. A commit
opens a details panel; branch buttons show only the commits a branch contains.

declarations.name: STATUSES
declarations.description:
Reads a job (CI run, pipeline, batch task) from JSON or a short text format, and
computes its progress and durations.

Text format:

```text
# Build and test
status: running

## Checkout
status: success
duration: 2s
Cloning into 'app'...

## Test
status: running
progress: 40
> vitest run
```

`# name` names the job, `## name` starts a step, `key: value` lines right after a heading
set its fields (`status`, `started`, `finished`, `duration`, `progress`), and every other
line is log text of the current step.

declarations.description:
Shows a job — a CI run, a pipeline, a batch task — with its progress, its steps and
their logs, like the job page of a CI service.

Reads JSON (`{ name, status, started, finished, progress, steps: [{ name, status,
started, finished, duration, progress, log }] }`) or a short text format where
`# name` names the job, `## name` starts a step and `status:`, `duration:` or
`progress:` lines set its fields. Each step opens to show its log with ANSI colors;
failed steps are open at first. `update()`, `setStep()` and `appendLog()` follow a
running job live.

declarations.description:
Displays JSON as highlighted text or as a collapsible tree.

The JSON is parsed by a built-in parser that keeps numbers exactly as written,
keeps duplicate keys, limits nesting depth and reports errors with line and column.
Everything is rendered with DOM text APIs: no HTML parsing is involved.

Decodes a JSON Web Token and shows its parts, header, payload and claims.

The token is only decoded: the signature is never verified, the token is never
sent anywhere, and URLs found in its header (`jku`, `x5u`) are never fetched.
Every value is rendered with DOM text APIs.

Displays application logs: levels, timestamps, structured fields and stack traces, with
level filters, a search that filters entries, and live streaming.

Plain text, JSON lines (pino, bunyan, winston, Logstash…) and logfmt are recognized
line by line. Stack traces and multi-line messages stay with their entry. ANSI colors
are shown. New lines can be streamed with `write()`, and the view follows them.

declarations.name: MAX_EQUATIONS
declarations.description: Equations per element.

declarations.name: splitEquations
declarations.description:
Equations of the content: blocks separated by blank lines, unless they are inside an
environment (`\begin{align}` … `\end{align}`) that spans them.

declarations.name: splitMath
declarations.description:
Splits text into text and math: `$$…$$` and `\[…\]` are display math, `$…$` and `\(…\)`
inline math. `\$` is a dollar sign; a `$` followed by a digit only closes math when it
opened some, so "$5 and $10" stays text.

declarations.name: parseMacros
declarations.description: Macros from JSON: `{"\\R": "\\mathbb{R}"}`. Names must be commands; definitions are text.

declarations.name: scrubMath
declarations.description:
Checks the MathML built by Temml before it reaches the page, the way the sanitizer checks
HTML: unknown elements are removed (their text kept), unknown attributes and any `href`
are removed, colors and lengths must be plain values, and inline styles keep only the
properties Temml uses, without `url()`.

declarations.description: The TeX of a rendered equation and its MathML, for copying.

so other modules do not carry them.

type.text: { ready: boolean, engine: MathEngine | null, promise: Promise<MathEngine> }

declarations.name: useMathEngine

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: Temml, or an object with its `render`.

declarations.description:
Uses a Temml that is already loaded (bundled with the page, or `import temml from 'temml'`)
instead of fetching dist/vendor/temml.js.

Shows math written in TeX, drawn by the browser as MathML: one equation, several
(separated by blank lines, optionally numbered), or text with math between `$…$`,
`$$…$$`, `\(…\)` and `\[…\]`. With `inline`, the element sits inside a line of text.

TeX is turned into MathML by Temml, loaded on demand (`dist/vendor/temml.js`). The MathML
is built with DOM methods, then checked against an allow-list of MathML elements,
attributes and styles; links, images and `\href` are never produced. Screen readers read
MathML natively, and the TeX is kept in an annotation.

declarations.name: en
declarations.description:
Interface strings of <vt-menu>, registered by its module with `defineStrings()`
so other modules do not carry them.

A menu of actions: a button that opens a menu (or a "⋮" button), a menu that opens on a
right click on an element of the page, or a list of actions always shown. Items come from
JSON or from lines of text: actions, links, check boxes, radio groups, headings,
separators, shortcuts, icons and submenus.

It follows the menu button pattern of WAI-ARIA: arrows, Home and End, letters to jump,
right and left for submenus, Escape to close, and the focus goes back where it was. The
menu stays inside the window, above or below its button.

their execution counts, and their outputs: text and errors with their ANSI colors, images,

as images, where they cannot run scripts.

declarations.name: METHODS
declarations.description:
Reads an OpenAPI 3.x (or Swagger 2.0) document into a model that is simple to display:
operations grouped by tag, parameters merged from the path and the operation, request
bodies and responses by media type, and helpers to resolve `$ref`, describe schemas and
build example values.

Only local references (`#/components/...`, `#/definitions/...`) are followed: external
files are never fetched. Every walk is bounded in depth and guarded against cycles.

declarations.name: MAX_OPERATIONS
declarations.description: Operations kept at most.

declarations.name: MAX_DEPTH
declarations.description: Deepest schema walked.
Thrown when the document is not OpenAPI.
declarations.name: SpecError
pointer
declarations.description: Follows a local JSON pointer (`#/components/schemas/User`).

declarations.name: resolve
declarations.description: Resolves `$ref` chains (at most 20 hops). Unknown references resolve to `null`.

declarations.name: refName
declarations.description: Name of the component a `$ref` points to (`User` for `#/components/schemas/User`).

declarations.name: readSpec
declarations.description: Reads an OpenAPI or Swagger document (already parsed from JSON or YAML).

declarations.name: mergeAllOf
declarations.description: Merges the schemas of `allOf` into one object schema (one level, references resolved).

declarations.name: typeLabel
declarations.description:
Short type label of a schema: `string (date-time)`, `integer`, `array of User`,
`User`, `"a" | "b"`, `one of: Cat, Dog`.

declarations.name: exampleFor
declarations.description:
Builds an example value for a schema: its `example`, `examples`, `default` or first
`enum` value, or a typical value for its type and format.

Documents an HTTP API from its OpenAPI description (3.0, 3.1, or Swagger 2.0), in JSON
or YAML: endpoints grouped by tag, parameters, request bodies, responses, schemas and
generated examples.

Every endpoint opens to show its details. With `<vt-http>` on the page, each endpoint
also gets an example request and response, with code for curl, fetch, Python and HTTPie.
Nothing is ever sent to the API.

declarations.description:
Shows a regular expression and what it matches: the pattern colored by part, an
explanation in plain words, the test text with every match and group marked, a table of
matches, and the result of a replacement.

In edit mode the pattern and the test text are edited live. Matching runs with limits:
at most 100,000 characters of text, 1,000 matches and 100 ms, checked between matches.
Patterns that repeat a repetition, like `(a+)+`, can take exponential time on a single
match: they only run after the reader asks.

declarations.name: en
declarations.description:
Interface strings of <vt-search>, registered by its module with `defineStrings()`
so other modules do not carry them.

A site search ready for a menu: a button with its keyboard shortcut opens a dialog that
searches as you type, results grouped by section with the words found highlighted, recent
searches and suggestions. It can also sit in the page as a search field.

Entries come from a JSON index (loaded the first time the search opens) or from your API.
Each entry has an id, such as a UUID: its address is its `url`, or `url-template` with
`{id}` replaced. Choosing a result fires a cancelable event, so a single-page app can route
it itself. Text is rendered with DOM text APIs, and addresses keep safe schemes only.

declarations.name: tokenize
declarations.description:
Splits SQL into tokens. Strings (`'…'`, `E'…'`, `$tag$…$tag$`), quoted names (`"…"`,
`` `…` ``, `[…]`) and comments are kept whole.

declarations.name: KEYWORDS
declarations.default: new Set( `select from where and or not in is null like ilike between exists as on join inner left right full outer cross natural using group by order having limit offset fetch first next rows only union all intersect except distinct insert into values update set delete returning with recursive create table view index unique primary key foreign references default check constraint drop alter add column rename to if case when then else end asc desc nulls last over partition window filter lateral true false begin commit rollback transaction grant revoke truncate cascade restrict materialized replace conflict do nothing explain analyze verbose temporary temp sequence schema database trigger function procedure returns language interval cast collate escape some any similar top percent ties merge matched`.split(/\s+/), )
declarations.description: Words shown in capitals by the layout.

declarations.name: formatSql
declarations.description:
Puts a query in a readable layout: keywords in capitals, one clause per line, the items
of a select list on lines of their own, conditions after `AND` / `OR` indented, and
subqueries indented. Comments, strings and names are kept as they are. Inside the
parentheses of a function call or a window (`OVER (PARTITION BY …)`) nothing moves.

declarations.default: { sqlQuery: 'Requête', sqlStatement: 'Instruction {index}', sqlResult: 'Résultat de l’instruction {index}', sqlRows: '{count} lignes', sqlRow: '1 ligne', sqlRowsShown: '{shown} lignes sur {count}', sqlNoRows: 'Aucune ligne', sqlParams: 'Paramètres', sqlError: 'Erreur', sqlFormat: 'Mettre en forme la requête', sqlAsWritten: 'Afficher la requête telle qu’écrite', sqlCopyQuery: 'Copier la requête', sqlCopyCsv: 'Copier en CSV', sqlDownloadCsv: 'Télécharger le CSV', sqlShowRows: 'Afficher {count} lignes de plus', sqlSortBy: 'Trier par {name}', sqlStatements: '{count} instructions', sqlInvalid: 'Ce JSON n’a pas pu être lu comme des résultats SQL : {message}', sqlNotRun: 'Affichage seulement : rien n’est envoyé à une base de données.', }

declarations.description:
Shows SQL queries and their results: a query alone, highlighted and laid out on demand;
a terminal session of psql, mysql, MariaDB, sqlite3 or DuckDB with its result tables;
or JSON (`{ query, params, columns, rows, rowCount, duration }`, a node-postgres result,
or a list of them).

Results are tables sorted by a click on a column, with `NULL` told apart from an empty
string, row counts, timings, errors and command tags. Nothing is ever run: the element
only reads text.

and days without data do not count; without `minutes`, a degraded day counts as up, a

declarations.description:
Interface strings of <vt-status>, registered by its module with `defineStrings()`
so other modules do not carry them.

Displays the status of a service: an overall banner, components with their uptime and a bar
per day, open incidents with their updates, scheduled maintenance and past incidents.

Reads its own JSON format or an Atlassian Statuspage summary (`/api/v2/summary.json`).
Every value is rendered with DOM text APIs, and links keep safe URL schemes only.

declarations.description:
A data table: typed sorting on several columns, filters per column, global search,
row selection with bulk actions, grouping, expandable rows, column chooser, resizing,
reordering and pinning, footer aggregates, cell editing, virtual scrolling,
keyboard navigation, export and a card layout on narrow screens.

Data comes from JSON (array of objects, array of arrays, or `{ columns, rows }`),
CSV / TSV text, or the `data` and `columns` properties. Cells are inserted as text.

declarations.name: TAG_EVENTS
declarations.description: Events specific to tags.

Displays, selects and creates tags.

Give it JSON — an array of tags, or `{ "value": [...], "options": [...] }` — and it shows
them as chips. With `mode="edit"` it becomes a form field: type with autocompletion,
use `#tag` syntax, paste lists, pick from a "browse all" panel, create new tags, and
get suggestions from a backend. The selection is submitted with the form as JSON.

A tag is a string, or an object:
`{ value, label, color, group, description, count, kind, href, disabled }`.

declarations.description:
Shows a terminal session: commands after their prompt, and their output with ANSI
colors.

Lines starting with a prompt (`$` by default) are commands: they are highlighted as
shell code and get their own copy button, which copies the command without the
prompt. Other lines are output, where ANSI colors, bold, underline, progress bars
(carriage returns) and OSC 8 links are rendered; other escape sequences are removed.

declarations.description:
Displays TOML as a collapsible tree or as highlighted text.

The TOML is read by a built-in TOML 1.0 parser: tables, arrays of tables, inline
tables, dotted keys, every string kind, integers in any base, floats, booleans,
dates and times. Duplicate keys and redefined tables are errors with line and
column. Values keep the text they were written with, and dates and times are shown
with their own type. Everything is rendered with DOM text APIs.

declarations.name: buildTree
declarations.description:
Links spans to their parents and orders them: each span before its children, children
by start time. Spans whose parent is missing become roots, marked as orphans; a cycle
of parents is broken the same way.

declarations.description: Time between ticks of the ruler, so that about `count` ticks fit: 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten.

declarations.name: tickLabel
declarations.description: A tick of the ruler, in a unit that fits the whole ruler: `0 ms`, `50 ms`, `1.5 ms`.

Shows a distributed trace as a waterfall: each span on its own row, indented under its
parent, with a bar for when it ran, its service and its duration. Choosing a span shows
its attributes, events and ids.

Reads OpenTelemetry traces (OTLP JSON, also one document per line as the collector's file
exporter writes them), Jaeger (UI download or API), Zipkin v2, or a plain list of spans
(`[{ id, parent, name, service, start, duration }]`, in milliseconds). A file with several
traces shows one at a time. Everything is shown as text; nothing is fetched.

declarations.name: en
declarations.description:
Interface strings of <vt-upload>, registered by its module with `defineStrings()`
so other modules do not carry them.

A field to add files: a zone where files are dropped, a button to choose them, and the list
of files with a thumbnail of images, their size and a button to remove them. Files are
checked against `accept`, `max-size` and `max-files`, and the ones refused say why.

It takes part in `<form>` like `<input type="file">`: the files are submitted under
`name`. With `upload-url`, each file is sent as soon as it is added, with its progress, and
the form submits what the server answered (an `id` or a `url`) instead of the file.

declarations.description:
Displays XML as a collapsible tree or as highlighted text.

The XML is read by a built-in parser as data only: nothing becomes a DOM node of the
page and nothing is fetched. The DOCTYPE is shown but never processed, so external
entities are never resolved and declared entities are never expanded. Nesting depth
and node count are limited, and errors are reported with line and column.
